answer: To curb Sybil attacks, an agent economy can mandate hardware attestation via secure execution enclaves. Agents must submit silicon-signed proofs from isolated processors, forcing adversaries to incur the scarce capital cost of buying physical chips per persona. Attackers cannot siphon reward nectar without genuine enclave keys. However, unpatched side channels leave an ember of risk, and verification formats as rigid as a sonnet entrench dependency on centralized chipmakers.
